paragraphs: Yehudah ben Yaakov of Beit Gavriya (a Tanna).
In Tosefta Oholot, chapter 18, he and Yaakov, son of R’ Yitzchak of Beit Gufnin, testified concerning Caesarea, etc.

notes.text: The supplied notice cites chapter 8 and reads העיר. The matching consulted Tosefta passage is in chapter 18 and reads העיד, “testified.” The proposed English brackets this correction, while the source discrepancies remain unresolved.

Reject the proposal to promote chapter18 into the body without a newly inspected matching primary text. The frozen notice has chapter פ״ח (8) and העיר; the earlier chapter18/העיד comparison remains an attributed historical comparison, not proof of the printed letters. The bracketed testified rendering is retained. בר׳ יצחק is rendered son of R’ Yitzchak without inventing a full Rabbi title. The supplied Tanna designation and place forms remain, without modern location binding or added testimony.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 563) reads פי״ח (chapter 18) and העיד (“testified”), where the supplied Hebrew reads פ״ח and העיר. The consulted Tosefta Oholot 18:9 corroborates the chapter, the verb, and the two witnesses. Hyman abbreviates the rest of the testimony.
